title: Inverse Design for Generating Initial Conditions in Scientific Simulations
problem: Scientific simulations governed by PDEs with time-evolving heterogeneous material interactions require appropriate initial conditions. Generating diverse sets of initial conditions reproducing observed output states (transient or steady) is challenging inverse problem.
motivation: Many scientific simulations require initial conditions matching observed phenomena. Traditionally, finding such conditions requires trial-and-error or expensive sampling. Generative models could efficiently sample from valid initial condition distributions.
method: Uses a conditional normalizing flow—a machine learning model trained to reverse the simulation process. Instead of starting with initial conditions and predicting outcomes (as typical simulations do), this model takes a target outcome and generates multiple different initial conditions that could produce it. Demonstrated on two physics problems—electrostatic potential (electric field behavior) and heat diffusion (temperature spreading)—showing it can rapidly generate diverse starting conditions for complex simulations.
key_novelty: Applying conditional normalizing flows to inverse design enables efficient generation of initial conditions from target simulation outputs.
contributions: Conditional normalizing flow framework for inverse design in PDEs
Two case study applications: electrostatic potential and heat diffusion
Comprehensive workflow documentation: synthetic datasets, model specification, training, evaluation
limitations: Abstract-only; specific PDE formulations, accuracy metrics, and comparison with alternative approaches not provided.
primary_theme: ML-based inverse design for scientific simulations
